title: Loop-current orderings in SU($N$) two-leg fermionic ladder through duality symmetries
authors: M. Habchy, F. Rose, P. Lecheminant
abstract: We investigate the formation of loop-current ordered phases in half-filled SU($N$) two-leg fermionic ladders. Using a low-energy approach, we uncover the existence of non-perturbative duality symmetries relating four competing orders. Two of these orders correspond to loop-current ordered phases that spontaneously break the time-reversal symmetry and describe charge currents circulating in a staggered pattern either around the plaquettes or along the diagonals of the ladder. These unconventional phases are shown to be dual to conventional (charge and bond) density-wave phases through an exact density-current duality symmetry existing on the lattice. From a perturbative renormalization group approach, we find that these phases for $N>2$ are stabilized in a half-filled SU($N$) two-leg Hubbard ladder with an additional SU($N$) Hund's interaction. The effect of a small doping on these phases is also discussed.
summary: This work theoretically analyzes the complex phase diagram of SU(N) two-leg fermionic ladders, focusing on the competition between conventional density-wave states and unconventional loop-current ordered phases. By utilizing advanced techniques like bosonization and duality symmetries, the authors demonstrate that these competing orders are mathematically linked, providing a unified framework for understanding electronic correlations in low-dimensional quantum materials.
main_problem: The study investigates loop-current ordered phases in half-filled SU(N) two-leg fermionic ladders and elucidates the relationship between these unconventional orders and conventional density-wave states via duality symmetries.
main_result: The model predicts four competing orders, showing that for N>2, loop-current phases are stabilized by Hund's interaction; furthermore, an exact density-current duality symmetry relates current-carrying phases to density-wave phases.
method: The analysis employs low-energy effective theories, renormalization group (RG) techniques, and bosonization methods applied to the continuum limit of the lattice Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is an SU(N) two-leg fermionic ladder described by a generalized Hubbard-type Hamiltonian incorporating hopping, on-site repulsion (U), interchain interactions (V, J_perp), and pair-hopping terms. The continuum limit yields massless Dirac fermions.
key_observables: Loop-current order parameters ($	ext{OAF}_\perp$, $	ext{OAF}_d$), conventional density-wave order parameters ($	ext{OCDW}^-$, $	ext{OBDW}$), and various current operators defining the symmetry algebra.
important_parameters: Half-filling, SU(N) structure, Hund's coupling ($J_\perp$), doping level, and interaction strengths (U, V).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on low-energy approximations, continuum limits, and the existence of specific duality symmetries ($D_{dc}$ and $D$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the two loop-current ordered phases breaking T-symmetry, the relationship between the four competing orders via duality symmetries, and the structure of the generalized SU(N) ladder Hamiltonian.
paper_structure: The paper moves from defining the full lattice Hamiltonian to deriving low-energy continuum descriptions using bosonization. It then systematically analyzes the symmetry constraints imposed by density-current dualities ($D_{dc}$), leading to a classification of the current algebra ($\mathfrak{so}(4N)$) and identifying which phases are stable under RG flow.
why_interesting: The deep connection established between exotic, time-reversal symmetry breaking loop currents and standard charge/bond density waves via exact duality symmetries provides powerful theoretical tools for understanding competing orders in strongly correlated materials.
